verdict.rationale: LibreOffice documents its own SDK, with API docs and a Developers Guide, plus a headless mode meant for external clients controlling it through the UNO API. That shows a vendor-provided programmatic interface, but the evidence never names specific language bindings, versioning or maintenance commitments. A community report of poor Python macro automation and missing JavaScript API docs for Calc suggests uneven language coverage. Missing for 10: explicit list of officially supported mainstream-language client libraries, versioning and release policy for those libraries, evidence of vendor maintenance, independent corroboration of a usable developer experience.

support.subject: As a developer, official client libraries exist for mainstream languages, versioned and maintained by the vendor

citations.quote: it is possible to use the SDK to develop an extension, for which you can read the API docs and Developers Guide.
This special mode can be used when the application is controlled by external clients via the API.
